clue.text: Tool making company located near golf club beyond the west end of Slough

indicators.note: the company is placed beyond, that is after, the letter from Slough
the golf club sits right next to the company, so the pieces run on side by side
in a word written left to right the west end is its first letter, so this takes the start of Slough

parts.note: a crew is a company of workers or sailors
a driver is the golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.surface: A tool-making firm has set up near a golf course on the edge of Slough.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a hand implement for turning screws, so it is a kind of tool.

clue.text: Head of Stonyhurst present at clog dance

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so this takes the start of Stonyhurst

parts.note: now means at present, in the current moment
to ball is to clog or clump, as wet snow packs into a horse's hoof

explanation.surface: The head teacher of Stonyhurst, a Catholic boarding school, turns up at a clog-dancing display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog dance' reads as one thing, but 'clog' is the wordplay and 'dance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a dance in which one couple starts and each partner picks a new one, so the floor fills up.

clue.text: Repaired last underlying crack caused by de-icer

indicators.note: in a down answer the shuffled letters lie under the crack piece, so they come after it

parts.note: rock is slang for crack cocaine

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters of last are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing the bottom layer of a cracked road surface was made necessary by the gritting.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse mineral salt is spread on winter roads to melt ice, so it serves as a de-icer.

clue.text: Quarrel about the Home Counties becoming less desirable

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for quarrel is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel
SE, south-east, stands for the Home Counties, the counties around London

explanation.surface: A dispute over the commuter belt around London makes the area a worse place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, meaning more unwelcome or less to be wished for.

clue.text: Cancel first of departures after bad weather's reported around South Carolina

indicators.note: the letter from departures comes after the rest
the sound-alike goes around the state's abbreviation, holding it inside
reported means said aloud, so the word for bad weather is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: rain is bad weather; the 's stands for is
SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

indicators.note: this takes the opening letter of departures

explanation.surface: An airport news item: departures are cancelled because heavy rain is reported over South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' works only on the weather word, before 'around' wraps it round the state; the 's of 'weather's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or order is to revoke it, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: French wine, say, starts to affect rotund American's vitality

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
e.g., for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken here from affect and rotund

explanation.surface: French wine, for instance, starts to sap a portly American's energy.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage vinegar means vigour or liveliness, as in the phrase full of vim and vinegar.

clue.text: Morally unprincipled salesman to steal money from pal

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rob is to steal

indicators.note: money is taken from the word for pal, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a mate is a pal
M is the abbreviation for money, as in £5m

explanation.surface: A crooked salesman sets out to swindle cash out of his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is someone without morals, and as an adjective it means depraved or unscrupulous.

clue.text: Try crack

definitions.meaning: to have a ... at something is to have a go, an attempt
a crack is a sharp bang, like the noise of a cork leaving a bottle

explanation.definitionFit: Pop is informal for an attempt, and also names a short explosive noise such as a crack.

clue.text: London district, trendy, not posh

indicators.note: not says the posh letter is left out of the word for trendy

parts.note: popular means fashionable, in favour
U means upper-class, posh, from the old U and non-U labels

explanation.surface: A part of London that is fashionable but not upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is a district in east London near Canary Wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is an area of the East End of London, in the borough of Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: Hospital worker left with Jerry regularly

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the letters from Jerry are joined straight on after the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth of Jerry

explanation.surface: A hospital staff member has gone off with someone called Jerry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital porter moves patients and equipment around the wards, so is a hospital worker.

clue.text: Come into the mind of old dog eating a piece of chicken

indicators.note: the dog eats the piece of chicken, so that letter goes inside it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: a piece here is just the first letter of chicken

explanation.surface: An elderly hound wolfing down a scrap of chicken pops into someone's thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is short for 'occur to', as in 'it didn't occur to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea occurs to you it enters your head or strikes you.

clue.text: Abrasive essay on French writer

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
a paper is an essay or academic article

explanation.surface: A hostile article written about a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' looks like an adjective describing the essay, but it is a noun: an abrasive is something used for scouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is grit-coated paper used for smoothing surfaces, a common abrasive.

clue.text: Crowding round to ask for housing — all the rage after German victory (or)

indicators.note: the word for ask for houses the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to beg is to ask for

indicators.note: the fashionable word comes after the German one

parts.note: Sieg is German for victory
in means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: A crowd begging for shelter, all furious after a German win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' splits the begging word after its second letter; the stray '(or)' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Besieging means surrounding a place with forces, so pressing in or crowding round it.

clue.text: Hold forth over top missing from packing case

parts.note: O stands for over, the cricket term

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which is lost from the packing case

parts.note: a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth about a packing case that has lost its lid.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a speech in a pompous way, which is to hold forth.

clue.text: Extremely petty over article looking into analysis of dill leaf

indicators.note: the reversed letters and the article look into, go inside, the rearranged dill
analysis breaks something down, so the letters of dill are taken apart and rearranged
over means turned over, so the two letters are read backwards
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here those of petty

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A very fussy look at the analysis of a dill leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysis of' rearranges the herb's letters to LILD, and the reversed pair with the article sits between its fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily.

clue.text: Plans for new pool pass without resistance

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the resistance symbol
making the letters new means arranging them afresh

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Designs for a new swimming pool get through planning without opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges POOLPASS into PROPOSALS without the R, which then goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposals are schemes or suggestions put forward for consideration, so they are plans.

clue.text: Study of English writer in recital

indicators.note: in a recital words are spoken aloud, so the writer's name stands for a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Charles Reade was an English novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth

explanation.surface: Reading up on an English author at a poetry reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university, as in reading law.

clue.text: Girl's to wait upon society swells

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, and Di's is its possessive
to tend is to attend to or wait upon

explanation.surface: A young woman means to serve as a waiter for high society's swells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swells' looks like a noun for posh people; it is a verb meaning bloats.
explanation.definitionFit: Distends means swells out by pressure from inside, as a stomach does after a big meal.

clue.text: Two features of good health

indicators.note: two copies of the facial feature are needed, so the word is written twice

parts.note: the chin is one of the features of the face

explanation.surface: Two signs that someone is in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' seems to mean characteristics; it means parts of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an old drinking toast, like saying cheers or your health.

clue.text: Soldiers involved in exercises in Dover

indicators.note: the soldiers are involved in the exercises, placed inside them

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercises
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are taking part in training drills down in Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dover' seems to be where the exercises happen; it is the definition, an example of a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a harbour town on the Kent coast, the main ferry point for crossings to France.

clue.text: Tailless dog lifted most of fish from cart

indicators.note: in a down answer lifted means turned upwards, so the docked dog is read backwards
without its tail the dog loses its last letter

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot

explanation.surface: A docked dog jumps up and steals most of a fish off a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: MUT reversed gives TUM; BRIL completes it. A tumbril carried victims to the guillotine in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbril is a two-wheeled tipping farm cart, famous for taking the condemned to execution.

clue.text: Mark's moral flaw

definitions.meaning: a mark here is a spot or stain on a surface
a moral flaw is a defect of character, a stain on someone's name

explanation.definitionFit: Blemish means both a physical spot that spoils appearance and a fault that spoils a reputation.

clue.text: Stupefies fellow doctors after uncertainty at the outset

indicators.note: the doctors come after the uncertainty letter

parts.note: Ben is a man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its first letter, here of uncertainty

parts.note: MBs are Bachelors of Medicine, qualified doctors

explanation.surface: A colleague stuns his fellow doctors after an early moment of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' reads as an adjective with doctors; it is a noun giving a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To benumb is to make numb or dull the senses, so to stupefy.

clue.text: Put an end to church tax earlier

indicators.note: the tax comes earlier, so it is placed before the church

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Abolish the church tax that came before.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it decisively, to finish it off.

clue.text: Broodingly resentful piece on the origins of the Easter Rising

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it, so the bit comes first

parts.note: a bit is a piece

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters, taken from the Easter Rising

explanation.surface: A grudging article written about how the 1916 Easter Rising began.
explanation.walkthrough: The Easter Rising was the 1916 Irish rebellion against British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter describes someone nursing a grudge, angry and resentful about past treatment.

clue.text: City in Colombia welcoming publicity

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the publicity goes inside the country's code

parts.note: CO is the international code for Colombia
air means airing, public exposure, as in getting air time

explanation.surface: A city in South America that welcomes media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in Colombia' reads as one phrase, but the city is in Egypt; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and one of the largest cities in Africa.

clue.text: Months that Anna wasted somewhere in New York

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for month

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Anna has wasted months in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is the central borough of New York City, so it is a place within New York.

clue.text: Liberal politician taken in by lie needs no introduction

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, which is dropped
the politician is taken in by the lie, placed inside it

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is fooled by a falsehood that needs no explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs no introduction' drops the first letter only after 'taken in by' has built TAMPLE. 'Liberal' looks like the party; it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean plentiful, as in liberal helpings, which is the sense of abundant here.

clue.text: Dali for instance created great art on Malta

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another comes after it
created means made up, so the letters of great art are formed into something new

parts.note: M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: Salvador Dali produced great paintings while staying on Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dali' looks like the Spanish painter; here it is just a word with four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, and DALI has four.

clue.text: Strike with low shot

definitions.meaning: to strike someone is to hit them with the fist
in golf or tennis a low, firm stroke kept down on a flat path

explanation.definitionFit: Punch means hitting with a fist, and in golf a punch shot is played low under the wind.

clue.text: His counterpart's a priestess of Aphrodite nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so the zero letter is taken off the priestess

parts.note: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite loved by Leander in Greek myth
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A male figure's opposite number is a priestess of the love goddess, no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' looks like the stock phrase 'no less'; it means remove O.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine pronoun is the counterpart of the masculine 'his', as in his and hers.

clue.text: Shop worker in South Africa facing reprimand over a couple of peeks at customer's bottom

indicators.note: South Africa faces the rest, standing in front of it
the reprimand is placed over the rest, covering it on both sides

parts.note: to be taught a lesson is to be reprimanded

indicators.note: the bottom letter sits right at the peek letters, joined on
a couple means two, so the first two letters of peeks
the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of customer's

explanation.surface: A South African shop assistant is told off for peeking at a customer's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: PE plus R goes inside LESSON to make LES-PER-SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesperson serves customers in a store, a shop assistant.
